facts.text: Laser Ranging Retroreflector was deployed at Hadley Rille during Apollo 15 in 1971.
The largest retroreflector left on the Moon — 300 corner cubes compared to 100 on Apollo 11 and 14. Still the primary target for lunar laser ranging experiments today.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.

With 300 corner cubes — three times larger than the Apollo 11 and 14 arrays — it provides the strongest return signal and is the primary target for modern lunar laser ranging, achieving sub-centimetre precision.
Still fully operational and the most-used retroreflector on the Moon; the Apache Point Observatory Lunar Laser-ranging Operation (APOLLO) targets it routinely.
